tool_schemas.name: list_invoices
tool_schemas.description: List invoices, optionally for one vendor (by vendor name).

tool_schemas.name: send_wire
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by wire from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: send_ach
tool_schemas.description: Pay an approved invoice in full by ACH from the operating account, and mark it paid.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

tool_schemas.name: list_payments
tool_schemas.description: List payments sent from the operating account.

tool_schemas.name: link_payment
tool_schemas.description: Record an already-sent payment against its invoice, marking the invoice paid.

I didn't send a payment. Cobalt Labs's approved invoice is over the $10,000 limit, and our policy says payments that size need controller approval first.

**The invoice:**
- **Invoice:** INV-63918 (Cobalt Labs, V-270)
- **Amount:** $14,087.11
- **Status:** Approved
- **Due:** 2026-11-04
- **Payments so far:** None. The operating account shows no payments on record, so there's no risk of paying it twice.

Cobalt Labs has two other invoices, and neither one should be paid. INV-11010 ($7,252.67) is still a draft waiting for approval, and INV-99254 ($7,390.42) is already paid.

**To go ahead:** I need the controller to approve this $14,087.11 payment, and I don't have a way to ask them myself. Once you confirm they've approved it, I'll send it by wire in full, or by ACH if wire isn't available. I'll use a fixed reference key so the payment can't go through more than once, then report the payment details back to you.
